clue.text: Vehicle in a million chap had taken, surprisingly

indicators.note: the vehicle sits inside the run formed by a, million and chap

parts.note: a chap is a man, referred to as he
a bus is a vehicle
D is the contracted form of had, as in I'd

explanation.surface: Someone driving a vehicle worth a million found it had been taken, to their surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: To be caught by surprise attack is to be waylaid, which is taken unawares.

clue.text: Opposed to soft cheeses that come in various flavours

definitions.note: the definition is a relative clause describing particles; the answer is a plural noun for them

parts.note: anti means opposed to
quark is a soft curd cheese

explanation.surface: Someone objects to soft cheeses sold in assorted flavours.
explanation.walkthrough: In particle physics quarks come in six 'flavours', so the cheese surface hides a physics definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In particle physics, the antiparticles of quarks are classified by flavour, like up, down and strange.

clue.text: One covered in scales, or feathers

definitions.meaning: a large constricting snake, whose skin is scaly
a long feathery scarf worn round the neck

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a scaly constricting snake and a fluffy feather stole.

clue.text: Promise to take in the sides of the garment

indicators.note: to take in means to enclose, so the promise word goes round the other letters

parts.note: to swear is to promise solemnly

indicators.note: the sides of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A tailor vows to take in the sides of a piece of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the sides of the' gives T and E, the first and last letters of 'the', which go inside SWEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A knitted top worn over a shirt is a common garment, especially in American usage.

clue.text: Doing this to Mr. 10 is fun

definitions.meaning: completes the title of Joe Orton's 1964 play about a lodger whose surname is the answer to 10 across

explanation.walkthrough: Mr. 10 points to the 10-across answer; Joe Orton's play title runs '... Mr' plus that surname, the missing first word being this answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something amusing or diverting is enjoyable to watch, which is what fun means here.

clue.text: Hearing a sketchy American speech

indicators.note: hearing signals that the words are to be taken by their sound

parts.note: sketchy means patchy, incomplete, so a sketchy is a patchy

explanation.surface: Someone listening to a rough American accent.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, 'a patchy' sounds like the language name.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Athabaskan language of a Native American people of the southwestern US.

clue.text: Child puts on light cloak

indicators.note: the child word is put on, that is attached to, the light word, coming after it

parts.note: pale means light in colour
a tot is a small child

explanation.surface: A youngster puts on a lightweight cloak.
explanation.definitionFit: A paletot is a loose outer coat or cloak, a word borrowed from French.

clue.text: Fey actor vainly cast

indicators.note: cast in the sense of thrown into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A whimsical performer has been chosen for a role without much point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' looks like theatre casting, fitting the actor, but it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Fey can mean having second sight, so a person with visionary powers is fey.

clue.text: Creeper climbed some way along piece of fencing

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means reading upwards, so the letters go backwards
only some way along the word is taken, a run of letters within it

explanation.surface: A climbing plant has crept part of the way along a stretch of fence.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Creeper' upwards as REPEERC; the run EPEE sits inside it. 'fencing' is the sport, not garden fencing.
explanation.definitionFit: The epee is one of the three swords used in the sport of fencing.

clue.text: Take off a garment and go out

indicators.note: out here means outside, so the go word is placed round the rest

parts.note: a go is a try, an attempt
a vest is a garment

explanation.surface: Someone is told to remove a garment and head outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take off' reads as removing clothes but is the noun take-off, a parody.
explanation.definitionFit: A take-off is a mocking imitation, and a grotesque parody is called a travesty.

clue.text: Upper-class townie's pounds grabbed by architect

indicators.note: the pounds are grabbed by, that is held within, the architect

parts.note: Sir John Soane was a Regency architect, designer of the Bank of England
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling

explanation.surface: A posh city dweller's money has been seized by an architect.
explanation.walkthrough: A Sloane Ranger is a stereotyped upper-class young Londoner from around Sloane Square in Chelsea.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for Sloane Ranger, the label for a fashionable, well-off young person in London.

clue.text: Some 600 feet from plug to device?

definitions.meaning: a nautical unit of distance, a tenth of a sea mile, about 600 feet
how far a flex stretches between the socket plug and the appliance

explanation.definitionFit: A nautical distance measure of about a tenth of a sea mile, read whimsically as a flex's length.

clue.text: Not even half competent officer?

parts.note: a quarter is less than half
a master is someone fully skilled, competent at something

explanation.surface: An officer who is less than half capable at his job.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface jibe at an incompetent officer splits into the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An army officer responsible for quarters and supplies, or a naval petty officer in charge of steering.

clue.text: Sky feature, Total Arts production, given to America

indicators.note: the America piece is given to, added to the end of, the rearranged letters
a production makes something new from the letters, so they are rearranged

parts.note: US is the United States of America

explanation.surface: A Total Arts show is handed over to an American audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'production' sounds theatrical next to 'Arts' but signals the anagram of TOTAL ARTS.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a uniform grey mid-level cloud sheet, a feature of the sky.

clue.text: Avoidance of extremes by medium formerly, with nothing to lose

parts.note: tempera is a painting medium using egg yolk

indicators.note: the formerly word has to lose a letter, which is removed

parts.note: once means formerly
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A spiritualist medium used to shun excess, having nothing to lose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'medium' suggests a spiritualist, but it is the painting medium. Removing O from ONCE leaves NCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Moderation and self-restraint, keeping clear of excess, is the virtue of temperance.

clue.text: It grows more quickly after the start

indicators.note: what is left after the start of the word has gone, so its first letter is dropped

parts.note: faster means more quickly

explanation.surface: A plant grows faster once it has got going.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping F, the first letter, from FASTER leaves the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A daisy-like garden flower is a plant, something that grows.

clue.text: Give out binder for elementary version

parts.note: to allot is to give out shares
rope binds things together

explanation.surface: Hand out a binder containing a simplified edition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elementary' means of a chemical element, not simple.
explanation.definitionFit: Each physical form of a chemical element, like diamond or graphite for carbon, is an allotrope.

clue.text: Accept senior office and salute the workers

parts.note: a kiss is a greeting or salute
hands are workers, as in farmhands

explanation.surface: A new boss takes up a senior post and greets the staff.
explanation.walkthrough: British ministers formally take office by kissing the monarch's hands.
explanation.definitionFit: The ceremony by which a British minister formally takes up office before the sovereign.

clue.text: The Avon in spate: that's unfortunate

definitions.note: used as a noun here, an unfortunate person

indicators.note: a river in spate is in flood and turbulent, so the letters are churned up

explanation.surface: The River Avon is flooding, which is bad luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in spate' fits the river, but it churns THE AVON into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A poor, deprived person lacking wealth is an unfortunate, used as a noun.

clue.text: Liable to cut music feature

definitions.meaning: the sign raising a note by a semitone

explanation.definitionFit: The word means keen-edged, and also names the notation that raises a note a semitone.

clue.text: A poser, but he'll put up bail to get you out

definitions.text: he'll put up bail to get you out
definitions.meaning: the wicketkeeper in cricket, who dislodges the bails to dismiss a batsman

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the wicketkeeper stumps a batsman by knocking the bails off; the surface suggests paying bail to free a prisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: A difficult question is a poser, and a cricket wicketkeeper is also called by this name.

clue.text: Boat a drain on funds?

definitions.meaning: an armed customs vessel used against smugglers
something that cuts into income, taken literally

explanation.definitionFit: This was an armed government vessel enforcing customs, but read literally it reduces income.

clue.text: Not good to clutch tool

indicators.note: not good means the good letter is removed from what follows

parts.note: to grasp is to clutch

explanation.surface: It is bad form to grip a tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A coarse file used for shaping wood or metal is a common tool.

clue.text: Conclusion of symphony by Bruckner, The Roman

indicators.note: by here means beside, so the closing letter follows the composer's name

parts.note: Anton Bruckner was the Austrian symphonist

indicators.note: the conclusion of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: The finale of a Bruckner symphony, called The Roman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Roman' is Mark Antony, Cleopatra's Roman lover, linking to 23 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark Antony was the Roman general, lover of Cleopatra.

clue.text: Like 22's lover to have tiny page redesigned

indicators.note: something redesigned is reshaped, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tiny page has been given a new design.
explanation.walkthrough: 22's lover is Cleopatra, queen of Egypt.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleopatra, beloved of Mark Antony, was the queen of Egypt and thus of that nationality.

clue.text: Annoy aircraftsman with speech

indicators.note: with speech signals the word is spoken and taken by sound

parts.note: erk is British RAF slang for a lowest-rank aircraftsman

explanation.surface: An airman annoys people when he speaks.
explanation.walkthrough: ERK is old RAF slang for a raw recruit; said aloud it gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To irritate or vex someone is to annoy them.

clue.text: Infatuation, wanting to hear this from Afghanistan

definitions.note: the definition describes the language one would hear spoken there

indicators.note: infatuation wanting 'to' means it needs the word to added after it

parts.note: pash is old schoolgirl slang for a crush or infatuation

explanation.surface: A crush makes someone long to hear something from Afghanistan.
explanation.definitionFit: This Iranian language is spoken by the Pashtun people and is an official language of Afghanistan.

clue.text: Constant man admired, endlessly eager and brave

parts.note: C is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light
a hero is a man who is admired

indicators.note: endlessly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: keen means eager

explanation.surface: A steadfast, admired man is endlessly keen and courageous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brave' is a noun here: a Native American warrior.
explanation.definitionFit: A brave is a Native American warrior, and this is one of the peoples of the southeastern US.
